time. 179 of the list's 425 European entries: 42 cement and 137 CO2 transport and
storage. The other 246 are refused by the perimeter on the publisher's own
Subsector and are DERIVED in sources/build_cement_ccs_benchmark.py rather than
listed here -- hand-listing 246 mechanical refusals would have invited a typo to
become a class.
KEYED BY THE IEA'S OWN `ID`, which is what the brief means by the benchmark's own
identifier. The key is a string because JSON keys are.
MATCHING TO A ROW IS BY COMPANY AND WORKS AGREEING, never by a name stem. That is
the batteries rule (sources/build_batteries_benchmark.py, 'MATCHING, AND WHAT IS
NOT A JOIN') and it is the only route used here. Every match is printed on every
run for confirmation. Where two objects look like one works and no source says so,
the pair goes to `reference_debts` and NOT into a join.
CAPACITY ON AN ADMITTED ROW IS THE OWNER'S FIGURE AT THE OWNER'S UNIT. Neither IEA
capacity column is ever written onto a row: 'Announced capacity' is the list's
claim and 'Estimated capacity by IEA' is the IEA's own computation through the
conversion factors on the workbook's Definitions tab. Where the two speakers
differ, the pair is recorded in `disagreements` and neither is reconciled.
A PHASE IS AN ENTRY. The IEA lists announced phases as separate rows with separate
IDs -- Viking CCS Phase 1/2/3, Northern Endurance 1/2/3, Aramis storage 1/2. The
gate sums to the list's entry count, so each phase takes its own class; where the
works is held here, every phase entry classes `held` and names the same row, on
the batteries precedent that one benchmark line over two held works is counted
once per LIST ENTRY and the reference is written onto the row.

725.ruling: RULED 15 September 2026, by George, on question Q3 of this census. THE CCS PERIMETER IS INFRASTRUCTURE FOR PERMANENT STORAGE AS ITS PURPOSE. Enhanced oil recovery injects CO2 in order to produce oil, and the IEA's own `Fate of carbon` column is the test: an entry whose fate is EOR is refused with this clause. The operator's own claim stays on the entry.

operator_claim.speaker: INA/MOL, own document
operator_claim.says: By application of the EOR project CO2 emissions will be significantly reduced (permanent disposal of 2.9 billion m3 CO2 or 5.4 million tonnes).

725.note:
THE OPERATOR CALLS IT PERMANENT DISPOSAL AND THE PUBLISHER CALLS IT EOR, and the ruling takes the publisher's column as the test rather than the operator's word for what the injection achieves. Both are recorded. This is the register's only European CO2 T&S entry with an EOR fate, and it is Operational, running since 2020 — so the exclusion removes a working installation from the sector rather than a plan, which is the case a reader should see the clause applied to.

THE SECOND EOR ENTRY IS ALREADY OUT ON A DIFFERENT CLAUSE AND STAYS THERE. IEA 669, MOL Szank field CO2 EOR in Hungary, also carries Fate of carbon = EOR, and its Subsector is Natural gas processing/LNG, so it is refused with 'capture, natural gas processing'. That clause is not replaced: the CCS perimeter's rule is that a refusal NAMES THE INDUSTRY because those entries are read later for the supplier nodes, and overwriting it with the EOR clause would throw the industry away to record a fate. The EOR fate is noted here instead.

BOTH APPEAR IN THE SECOND LIST TOO. The CO2RE capture filed for this census shows 'MOL Szank Field CO2-EOR Site (HUN), Operational, 1992' and 'INA/MOL CO2 EOR Croatia (HRV), Operational, 2014' among the ten European rows it renders — which is the only use this register has been able to make of that list.
